title: Global Trends: Paradox of Progress
notes: Cover date January 2017; public release reported as 9 January 2017 (day not verified in this capture). Sixth edition. The title carries no year (the Chairman's letter says a year would convey 'a false precision'); the report frames its trends 'Through 2035' and its scenarios over a 20-year horizon, so target_year 2035 is used for scenarios. Scope: the three scenarios (Islands, Orbits, Communities) and dated or quantified projections the NIC states in its own voice in 'The Future Summarized' and the 'Trends Transforming the Global Landscape' section. The five-year regional outlooks ('Near-Future of Rising Tensions') and the annexes were not mined. Figures the NIC attributes to others (UN: half of world population facing water shortages by 2035; urbanization to two-thirds by 2050; a study on women's economic roles) are excluded. dni.gov returns 403 to scripts; read from the Wayback copy.

entries.label: Next five years: rising tensions, slower global growth
entries.quote: The next five years will see rising tensions within and between countries. Global growth will slow, just as increasingly complex global challenges impend.
entries.subject: global economic growth
entries.note: The Future Summarized, p. ix. 'Next five years' from January 2017.

entries.label: Terrorism threat expands in coming decades
entries.quote: The threat from terrorism will expand in the coming decades as the growing prominence of small groups and individuals use new technologies, ideas, and relationships to their advantage.
entries.subject: terrorism
entries.note: The Future Summarized, pp. ix-x. 'Coming decades' has no end year; 2035 is the report frame.

entries.label: Interstate conflict risk at levels not seen since the Cold War
entries.quote: Overconfidence that material strength can manage escalation will increase the risks of interstate conflict to levels not seen since the Cold War.
entries.subject: great power conflict
entries.note: The Future Summarized, p. x. In the passage on the 'dark and difficult near future'; read as the five-year outlook (to 2022). Low certainty on the horizon.

entries.label: World population 8.8 billion by 2035
entries.quote: The world population is forecasted to jump from roughly 7.3 to 8.8 billion people by 2035.
entries.subject: world population
entries.note: Key trends, 'The Rich Are Aging, The Poor Are Not', p. 8. Passive voice; forecaster not named.

entries.label: Median ages peak by 2035 in Japan, South Korea, Germany and others
entries.quote: Median ages will reach highs by 2035 in Japan (52.4), South Korea (49.4), Germany (49.6), and in several other countries. Europe will be hit especially hard, as well as Cuba (48), Russia (43.6), and China (45.7).
entries.subject: population aging
entries.value: Japan 52.4; South Korea 49.4; Germany 49.6; Cuba 48; Russia 43.6; China 45.7

entries.label: US median age about 41 by 2035
entries.quote: The United States is aging at a slower rate—reaching a median age of approximately 41 by 2035—and will maintain a growing working-age population.
entries.subject: population aging

entries.label: More than 30 countries in extremely high water stress by 2035
entries.quote: More than 30 countries—nearly half of them in the Middle East—will experience extremely high water stress by 2035, increasing economic, social and political tensions.
entries.subject: water scarcity
entries.metric: countries with extremely high water stress
entries.note: Key trends, environment. The preceding bullet (half of world population facing water shortages by 2035) is attributed to the UN and not captured.

entries.label: Nuclear weapon states maintain or modernize forces to 2035
entries.quote: Current nuclear weapon states will almost certainly continue to maintain, if not modernize, their nuclear forces out to 2035.
entries.subject: nuclear weapons

entries.label: Shia-Sunni schism and violent religious nationalism may not abate by 2035
entries.quote: schism between Shia and Sunni are likely to worsen in the short term and may not abate by 2035.
entries.subject: terrorism
entries.note: Key trends, terrorism, pp. 40-41. Full sentence (split by a page break): 'the rise of violent religious nationalism and the schism between Shia and Sunni are likely to worsen in the short term and may not abate by 2035.'

entries.label: Islands
entries.quote: Islands investigates a restructuring of the global economy that leads to long periods of slow or no growth, challenging both traditional models of economic prosperity and the presumption that globalization will continue to expand.
entries.subject: global economy
entries.note: The Future Summarized, p. xi. National-level response to volatility: protectionism and turning inward versus new sources of growth.

entries.label: Orbits
entries.quote: Orbits explores a future of tensions created by competing major powers seeking their own spheres of influence while attempting to maintain stability at home.
entries.subject: great power conflict
entries.note: The Future Summarized, p. xi. Regional level. Features a nuclear weapon used in anger, after which use is not repeated.

entries.label: Communities
entries.quote: Communities shows how growing public expectations but diminishing capacity of national governments open space for local governments and private actors, challenging traditional assumptions about what governing means.
entries.subject: governance
entries.note: The Future Summarized, p. xi. Sub-state and transnational level; companies, advocacy groups, charities and local governments outperform national governments.
